source.title: Geometric Similarity in VLM Low-Level Vision Representations
source.authors: Shao-Jun Xia; Hui-Xin Zhang; Zhen Lei; An-Lan Sun; Yun-Er Zhang; Xiao-Yang Chen

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE-derived sparse features in low-level vision representations of VLMs, a new setting for indirect evidence about sparse features in real models. It does not test toy-model superposition or capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The paper measures task-conditioned VLM representations and SAE features, not whether networks with more sparse features than dimensions superpose them rather than drop them. It does not vary feature sparsity or importance, measure neuron polysemanticity, or identify 1-D directions as the units of superposition. General task-geometry metrics and cited results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAEs as an analysis tool on task-minus-neutral hidden-state displacements in seven VLMs. It reports task-selectivity and cross-model distribution statistics of the SAE features. It does not test whether sparse features exist or are superposed, whether SAEs recover real model features, or anything about neuron polysemanticity, capacity, or feature dimensionality. The only reconstruction number (explained variance ≥ 0.80) is an eligibility criterion the authors imposed when choosing λ and accepting seeds. It is not a measured outcome.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct, but incomplete. The authors' main conclusion concerns geometry, not SAEs. Low-level tasks have stable within-task geometry, and cross-model universality is mainly global (mean dCor 0.77) rather than local (NNGS 0.27; PAR above baseline for 16 of 21 pairs). Task structure is mechanism-centric rather than family-based. SAE features are broadly reused within models, and feature-level cross-model sharing needs explicit validation.
record.recipe_differences: No superposition recipe is applied; the study uses observational hidden-state measurements and SAE decomposition.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors note dependence on SAE dictionary size and sparsity regularization, stable-layer selection, and other analysis choices; they call for validation across layers, methods, and model pairs.

fits_no_version.finding: Within each VLM, only 0.9–15.1% of live SAE features are task-specific (TSI > 0.85), while 13.4–72.4% are shared (TSI < 0.30). The authors read this as broad feature reuse across low-level tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features of VLM low-level-task representations are mostly reused across tasks rather than task-specific.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-task cross-model SAE activation-rate MMD falls below the within-model different-task reference for only 6 of 21 model pairs, and for only 3 of 21 consistently across all seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model similarity of SAE activation-rate distributions is limited and pair-specific.

record.code_released: The text says the code is available on GitHub but does not state a URL.
record.problems: The paper studies VLM low-level vision representations rather than LLM language representations or toy networks. SAE findings depend on dictionary and regularization choices; the authors also note single-layer analysis and the need for further validation. Reconstruction quality alone does not establish that the learned features are complete or canonical.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results left out. The cross-model activation-rate MMD finding is recorded under fits_no_version because it does not measure any listed version's named behavior.

untested.parts: All: no toy networks, no sparsity or importance manipulation, no geometry of superposed directions.
All: no capacity competition and no neuron polysemanticity measured.
All: no alternative causes of polysemanticity examined.
All: SAE reconstruction quality is a selection constraint, not a finding. There is no test of feature interpretability or of features spread across neurons.
All: cross-model MMD compares unaligned activation-rate distributions and does not test completeness, stability or canonicity of features.
All: dimensionality of features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's fits_no_version entry referenced a nonexistent row r4; it is fixed here to point to r2/r3, with an empty row list for the MMD finding. The SAE inputs are differences between task-prompt and neutral-prompt last-token states, not standard residual activations. This further distances the study from the claims about how models store features. Its single 'supports' label for V4 rested on an imposed selection threshold and on task-selectivity statistics, so it is removed.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature-over-dimension capacity, overlapping nearly orthogonal directions, and sparsity-dependent geometric transitions.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Alternative causes of polysemantic neurons and whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests low-level vision representations in VLMs, not language-model representations generally; does not test features spread across neurons.
Does not establish whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units; it compares activation-rate distributions rather than individual feature correspondence.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: seven VLMs (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Models range from approximately 7–8B to greater than 13B; individual sizes not stated for this aggregate
rows.operation_detail: Measured held-out SAE reconstruction quality; all final seeds were required to meet the explained-variance check.

conditions.value: stable-layer representations across 24 low-level vision tasks

rows.value: explained variance ≥ 0.80 (required check; all seeds must satisfy it)
rows.note: This is evidence that the trained dictionaries reconstruct the measured representations to the stated threshold; it does not establish that SAE features are complete or canonical model units.
rows.check: This is a selection value, not a result. λ was chosen so candidates meet explained variance ≥ 0.80 and seeds had to pass the same check (Appendix C.3), so the value is guaranteed by construction. It also applies to task-minus-neutral displacement vectors, not raw activations. It should not be a row.

rows.subject: seven VLMs (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Models range from approximately 7–8B to greater than 13B; individual sizes not stated for this aggregate
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of live SAE features classified as task-specific.

conditions.value: stable-layer representations across 24 low-level vision tasks

rows.measure: fraction of live SAE features classified as task-specific
rows.note: The range is reported across models, not as an individual result for each model.
rows.check: The fraction of task-specific features (0.9–15.1%) measures how SAE features are spread across the 24 low-level tasks. It does not measure whether the model contains recoverable sparse features or spreads features across neurons, so it does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: seven VLMs (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: Models range from approximately 7–8B to greater than 13B; individual sizes not stated for this aggregate
rows.operation_detail: Measured the fraction of live SAE features classified as shared across tasks.

conditions.value: stable-layer representations across 24 low-level vision tasks

rows.measure: fraction of live SAE features classified as shared
rows.note: The range is reported across models, not as an individual result for each model.
rows.check: The shared-feature fraction (13.4–72.4%) measures feature reuse across tasks, a construct different from any version. The definition depends on the TSI threshold and on SAE choices.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SAE decomposition of low-level vision representations in the seven tested VLMs
reader_labels.reason: The dictionaries meet the stated reconstruction check, and the study reports live features with task-specific and shared activation patterns (r1–r3). This supports the SAE-feature part of V4 in this setting, not its broader LLM or neuron-distribution wording.
